title: Fluid radius and contrast mapping for analytics cards and dense tables
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: Several analytics surfaces (cards, table rows, and dense chart widgets) render inconsistently across breakpoints: radii feel too large at compact widths, shadows either flatten or become visually noisy at high contrast, and accent colors used for data markers lose legibility in low-contrast themes. This ticket defines a token-led approach to: 1) introduce a fluid radius system tied to density tokens, 2) add a two-axis elevation matrix (depth x emphasis) for shadow layering, 3) create contrast-mapped accent aliases for chart/data colors to guarantee WCAG AA on foreground content, and 4) provide a migration path that minimizes churn for component teams.

migration_steps: 1) Introduce new tokens in token package as aliases (radius.container, radius.control, elevation.depth-1-emphasis-low).
2) Add backward-compatible CSS variable aliases for legacy names (--radius-md -> --r-radius-control) for one release cycle.
3) Ship a small codemod to update import points and component styles in consuming repos (script + preview).
4) ENG to implement runtime theme flag for canary rollout to 10% of traffic on dedicated and hosted consoles.
5) QA: run visual diffs for cards/tables/charts across breakpoints and high-contrast mode; evaluate perf for repaint boundaries.
6) Deprecate legacy variables after two sprints; provide rollback instructions and short-term mitigation for partners.
qa_checklist: Visual diff baseline for desktop/tablet/mobile at three widths
Contrast check for all chart marker/label combinations against background tokens
Interaction test: focus rings and overlays with new radius values
Performance: ensure shadow layering does not increase paint time >5% on dashboards
Regression: run unit snapshots for 42 affected components
